text:
maria: Running into a weird onboarding friction: sample app upload endpoint sometimes fires twice when user backs out quickly on Pixel 7 / Android 13. Backend sees two POSTs ~500ms apart.

maria: Using Retrofit suspend functions + OkHttp 4.10.0. Not reproducible on emulator or older phones.

tom: That sounds like a cancellation race where coroutine cancellation doesn't propagate to the underlying OkHttp Call in time. Which Retrofit adapter/version?

maria: Retrofit 2.9.0, Kotlin 1.8.20. The sample uses a streaming RequestBody for the image.

anya: Streaming bodies are the usual suspect. If the client cancels while the RequestBody is being written, OkHttp might already have flushed the request to the socket. Server will have received it and processed it, while client thinks it cancelled.

tom: Quick mitigation: buffer the body for small uploads in onboarding (use RequestBody.create(MediaType, byte[]) instead of streaming) or write a small wrapper that cancels the Call on job completion:```kotlin
val call = service.rawUploadCall(body)
job.invokeOnCompletion { call.cancel() }
call.await() // adapter
```

maria: Tried the cancel binding and buffering the body, greatly reduced duplicates. Still saw one case where two requests happened on Pixel 7 Pro.

anya: Also add `okhttpClientBuilder.retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for the sample to avoid hidden retries in race windows.

tom: For parity, Java enqueue/cancel semantics differ from the suspend adapter. Add a short note in SDK docs: "cancellation semantics differ across call paths; prefer buffered bodies for onboarding samples; bind coroutine Job -> OkHttp Call for robust cancellation."

build-bot: CI run created: https://ci.internal/repro/1759998765-1 (device matrix: Pixel6a/7/7Pro API 31/33).

maria: Filing a small repro and PR to change sample to buffered uploads + call.cancel wiring + update docs. Will include a tiny test that cancels after 10ms in device CI to catch regressions.

tom: Great — add note on HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 too (some devices prefer h2 and behaviour varies under proxy). Also recommend callTimeout to bound send durations.

maria: Adding all that to the PR. Thanks!
